narrative.intro: OptumServe Health Services had $1.9B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date across 14 awards, with an average award size of $137M. Obligations were down 24.5% year over year. The Department of Veterans Affairs was the dominant buyer, accounting for $1.9B of obligations in FY2026 to date. Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) was the largest NAICS market with $1.9B in obligations, followed by Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists at $11M and All Other Outpatient Care Centers at $10.8M. Historical obligations show a multi-year rise and fall pattern: FY21 $756M, FY22 $874M, FY23 $711M, FY24 $1.6B, FY25 $2.5B, and FY26 $1.9B. Smaller buying agencies in FY2026 to date include the Department of Defense with $16.3M and the Department of Health and Human Services with $11.5M. These figures are fiscal year to date totals and represent contract obligations rather than total potential contract value.

sections.heading: How concentrated are OptumServe Health Services obligations by agency?
sections.body: The Department of Veterans Affairs obligated $1.9B to OptumServe Health Services in FY2026 to date, making VA by far the largest buyer. The Department of Defense obligated $16.3M and the Department of Health and Human Services obligated $11.5M. This means VA accounts for the vast majority of FY2026 to date obligations.

sections.heading: What markets and contract sizes drive OptumServe Health Services revenue?
sections.body: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) generated $1.9B in obligations in FY2026 to date, making that NAICS market the primary source of obligations. Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists accounted for $11M and All Other Outpatient Care Centers accounted for $10.8M. The company had 14 awards in FY2026 to date with an average award size of $137M.

faq.q: How much does OptumServe Health Services make from federal contracts?
faq.a: OptumServe Health Services had $1.9B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company recorded 14 awards in FY2026 to date with an average award size of $137M, and obligations were down 24.5% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from OptumServe Health Services?
faq.a: The Department of Veterans Affairs is the largest buyer, obligating $1.9B to OptumServe Health Services in FY2026 to date. The Department of Defense obligated $16.3M and the Department of Health and Human Services obligated $11.5M in FY2026 to date.

faq.q: What does OptumServe Health Services sell to the government?
faq.a: OptumServe Health Services sells physician and outpatient care services to the government, with Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) accounting for $1.9B in FY2026 to date obligations. Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists generated $11M and All Other Outpatient Care Centers generated $10.8M in FY2026 to date obligations.

faq.q: Which OptumServe Health Services contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: No expiring contracts are listed for OptumServe Health Services in the provided FY2026 to date figures. The available tables report current obligations, top markets, and historical obligations but do not show expiring-contract details.
